newsitem.title: USA: US Northeast daily power prices flat on mild temps.
newsitem.headline: US Northeast daily power prices flat on mild temps.

text.p: Bulk electricity prices for Thursday in the northeastern U.S. were unchanged Wednesday amid mild temperatures and a lack of heating demand in the region.
"It's pretty much the same (price level as on Tuesday)," said a New York electricity trader.
Peak, non-firm electricity prices (including transmission) for Thursday in the eastern half of the New York Power Pool (NYPP) stayed in a $26.00-$30.00 a megawatt hour (MWh) range.
Off-peak, non-firm power for day-ahead delivery in eastern NYPP remained at $23.00-$24.00.

Con Edison was said to be an active power buyer in the hourly market. Its 975 megawatt (MW) Indian Point nuclear unit 2 remained shut after it was out of service January 18 to correct problems with a feedwater valve.
No startup date has been scheduled. Con Edison awaits a meeting with the Nuclear Regulatory Commission before restart.

A second nuclear unit at the Indian Point nuclear complex north of New York City was still off line. The 965 MW unit 3, operated by the New York Power Authority, was expected to remain idled at least through mid-February for replacement work in its primary containment area.
In western NYPP, peak, non-firm power for Thursday was quoted again at $20.00-$24.00.
Western NYPP electricity for off-peak, non-firm delivery Thursday remained at $16.00-$18.00.
In the New England Power Pool (NEPOOL), peak, non-firm electricity prices for Thursday at Northeast Utilities' (NU) border was still holding at $32.00-$35.00.
Non-firm, off-peak NEPOOL power for next-day delivery at the NU border stayed in a $25.00-$28.00 range.

Although temperatures are expected to dip in parts of the Northeast tomorrow, readings are likely to continue to average slightly above normal, edging up Sunday with chance of snow in the northern section a week from now.
Swing natural gas values at the New York City gate stayed at the $3.00 per million British thermal unit level.
